Signs of the World

Stop

History

The first stop sign was created in 1914 by Harold Jackson, a Detroit police sergeant who wanted to slow traffic entering an intersection. It gained widespread adoption throughout Michigan the following year. The modern specification was first published in 1935 in the US Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD). The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals specifies two stop signs, a red octagon and a circle with a red border.

Adoption

The red octagon is widely adopted around the world. As of 2024, there are only a few exceptions. Japan uses a triangular sign. Cuba, Madagascar, and Pakistan use circular signs.
